557	    def pull_queue(
558	        self, execution_id: str, name: str, raw: Any, key: str | None, tenant: str = DEFAULT_TENANT
559	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
560	        self._empty_body(raw, "pull")
561	
562	        def apply() -> dict[str, Any]:
563	            self.get_execution(execution_id, tenant)
564	            queue_row = self._queue_row(execution_id, name, tenant)
565	            if queue_row is None:
566	                raise NotFoundError(f"queue {name} was not found for execution {execution_id}")
567	            subscription = self.store.decode(queue_row["document"])
568	            visibility = subscription["visibility_seconds"]
569	            now = time.time()
570	            delivered = []
571	            for message_row in self._queue_message_rows(execution_id, name, tenant):
572	                message = self.store.decode(message_row["document"])
573	                if self._effective_queue_status(message, now) != "pending":
574	                    continue
575	                # The message leaves the pending set until the visibility
576	                # deadline; unacknowledged by then, it becomes pending again.
577	                message["status"] = "delivered"
578	                message["invisible_until"] = now + visibility
579	                message["delivery_count"] += 1
580	                message["deliveries"].append(
581	                    {"delivered_at": self.store.now(), "delivery": message["delivery_count"]}
582	                )
583	                self.store.connection.execute(
584	                    "UPDATE queue_messages SET document = ? "
585	                    "WHERE tenant = ? AND execution_id = ? AND queue = ? AND sequence = ?",
586	                    (self.store.encode(message), tenant, execution_id, name, message_row["sequence"]),
587	                )
588	                # Every delivery to the caller is metered as a delivery
589	                # attempt, atomically with the pull that made it.
590	                self._record_usage(tenant, USAGE_TYPE_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTED)
591	                delivered.append(self._render_queue_message(message_row["sequence"], message, now))
592	            # An empty queue (or one with nothing currently deliverable) is a
593	            # definite empty result, not an error.
594	            return {"messages": delivered}
595	
596	        with self._operation():
597	            return self._idempotent(key, f"pull-queue:{execution_id}:{name}", apply, tenant)
598	
599	    def ack_queue(
600	        self, execution_id: str, name: str, raw: Any, key: str | None, tenant: str = DEFAULT_TENANT
601	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
602	        if not isinstance(raw, dict) or set(raw) != {"idempotency_key"}:
603	            raise ValidationError("ack body must contain exactly an idempotency_key string")
604	        idempotency_key = raw["idempotency_key"]
605	        if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
606	            raise ValidationError("ack idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
607	
608	        def apply() -> dict[str, Any]:
609	            self.get_execution(execution_id, tenant)
610	            if self._queue_row(execution_id, name, tenant) is None:
611	                raise NotFoundError(f"queue {name} was not found for execution {execution_id}")
612	            for message_row in self._queue_message_rows(execution_id, name, tenant):
613	                message = self.store.decode(message_row["document"])
614	                if message["idempotency_key"] != idempotency_key:
615	                    continue
616	                if message["status"] == "acknowledged":
617	                    # A repeated acknowledgement names a message that already
618	                    # left the queue: it is missing, like an unknown key.
619	                    raise NotFoundError(f"queue message {idempotency_key} was not found")
620	                message["status"] = "acknowledged"
621	                message["invisible_until"] = None
622	                self.store.connection.execute(
623	                    "UPDATE queue_messages SET document = ? "
624	                    "WHERE tenant = ? AND execution_id = ? AND queue = ? AND sequence = ?",
625	                    (self.store.encode(message), tenant, execution_id, name, message_row["sequence"]),
626	                )
627	                return {"acknowledged": True}
628	            raise NotFoundError(f"queue message {idempotency_key} was not found")
629	
630	        with self._operation():
631	            return self._idempotent(key, f"ack-queue:{execution_id}:{name}", apply, tenant)

717	    # --- operational metrics ---------------------------------------------
718	
719	    def metrics(
720	        self,
721	        tenant: str,
722	        since: datetime | None = None,
723	        until: datetime | None = None,
724	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
725	        """Aggregate the tenant's persisted business facts into run metrics.
726	
727	        The query is read-only: it appends no events, writes no usage records,
728	        and settles nothing (a due timeout stays unsettled until an operation
729	        observes it), so the answer reflects exactly what is stored. Every
730	        dimension is always present — a tenant with no recorded facts gets a
731	        definite all-zero result rather than an error.
732	
733	        ``since`` and ``until`` bound a closed interval on the facts'
734	        occurrence times: a fact whose time equals either endpoint is counted.
735	        A window with ``since`` later than ``until`` simply contains no facts,
736	        so every dimension reports zero.
737	        """
738	        if not tenant:
739	            raise ValidationError("tenant id must be a non-empty string")
740	        with self._operation():
741	            with self.store.transaction():
742	                return self._metrics_counts(tenant, since, until)
743	
744	    def _metrics_counts(
745	        self,
746	        tenant: str,
747	        since: datetime | None,
748	        until: datetime | None,
749	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
750	        """Compute the metrics document; the caller validates the tenant and holds a transaction."""
751	        # A window with since later than until contains no facts at all, so its
752	        # result is the same definite zero shape as a tenant with no facts.
753	        empty_window = since is not None and until is not None and since > until
754	
755	        distribution: dict[str, Any] = {
756	            "running": 0,
757	            "completed": 0,
758	            "terminated": {reason: 0 for reason in TERMINATION_REASONS},
759	        }
760	        # Each execution contributes exactly one status fact: a running
761	        # execution's fact is its execution_started event, while a completed or
762	        # terminated execution's fact is the event that established that
763	        # status. With no window this counts every execution once, exactly as
764	        # the unfiltered baseline does. An execution has at most one terminal
765	        # event, so the join never multiplies rows.
766	        if not empty_window:
767	            status_rows = self.store.connection.execute(
768	                "SELECT e.state, COALESCE(t.occurred_at, s.occurred_at) AS at "
769	                "FROM executions e "
770	                "JOIN events s ON s.tenant = e.tenant AND s.execution_id = e.id AND s.type = 'execution_started' "
771	                "LEFT JOIN events t ON t.tenant = e.tenant AND t.execution_id = e.id "
772	                "AND t.type IN ('execution_completed', 'execution_terminated') "
773	                "WHERE e.tenant = ?",
774	                (tenant,),
775	            ).fetchall()
776	            for row in status_rows:
777	                if not self._within_window(_parse_stored_time(row["at"]), since, until):
778	                    continue
779	                state = self.store.decode(row["state"])
780	                status = state["status"]
781	                if status == "terminated":
782	                    reason = state.get("termination_reason")
783	                    if reason in distribution["terminated"]:
784	                        distribution["terminated"][reason] += 1
785	                elif status in ("running", "completed"):
786	                    distribution[status] += 1
787	
788	        # Completion, failure, and retry consumption are counted from
789	        # the recorded node events: condition evaluations and skips
790	        # append their own event types and are never counted here, and
791	        # loop body nodes accumulate one event per iteration. A version
792	        # migration appends no node events, so facts recorded before
793	        # and after it accumulate under the same node identifiers.
794	        completions: dict[str, int] = {}
795	        failures: dict[str, int] = {}
796	        retries: dict[str, int] = {}
797	        buckets = {
798	            "node_completed": completions,
799	            "node_failed": failures,
800	            "node_retried": retries,
801	        }
802	        if not empty_window:
803	            rows = self.store.connection.execute(
804	                "SELECT type, payload, occurred_at FROM events WHERE tenant = ? "
805	                "AND type IN ('node_completed', 'node_failed', 'node_retried')",
806	                (tenant,),
807	            ).fetchall()
808	            for row in rows:
809	                if not self._within_window(_parse_stored_time(row["occurred_at"]), since, until):
810	                    continue
811	                node_id = self.store.decode(row["payload"])["node_id"]
812	                bucket = buckets[row["type"]]
813	                bucket[node_id] = bucket.get(node_id, 0) + 1
814	
815	        # Delivery outcomes are counted per outbound HTTP attempt, so
816	        # a delivery that fails and then succeeds on a retry records
817	        # one of each; an attempt succeeded exactly when it received a
818	        # 2xx status code. A delivery document carries the single
819	        # occurred_at of the delivery record, shared by every attempt
820	        # recorded in it.
821	        succeeded = 0
822	        failed = 0
823	        if not empty_window:
824	            rows = self.store.connection.execute(
825	                "SELECT document FROM deliveries WHERE tenant = ?",
826	                (tenant,),
827	            ).fetchall()
828	            for row in rows:
829	                document = self.store.decode(row["document"])
830	                if since is not None or until is not None:
831	                    occurred_at = document.get("occurred_at")
832	                    if not isinstance(occurred_at, str) or not self._within_window(
833	                        _parse_stored_time(occurred_at), since, until
834	                    ):
835	                        continue
836	                attempts = document.get("attempts")
837	                if not isinstance(attempts, list):
838	                    continue
839	                for attempt in attempts:
840	                    status_code = attempt.get("status_code") if isinstance(attempt, dict) else None
841	                    if isinstance(status_code, int) and 200 <= status_code < 300:
842	                        succeeded += 1
843	                    else:
844	                        failed += 1
845	
846	        # One trigger row exists per settled schedule period, so a
847	        # repeated settlement of the same period counts nothing more.
848	        triggers: dict[str, int] = {}
849	        if not empty_window:
850	            rows = self.store.connection.execute(
851	                "SELECT workflow_id, triggered_at, COUNT(*) AS count FROM schedule_triggers "
852	                "WHERE tenant = ? GROUP BY workflow_id, triggered_at ORDER BY workflow_id",
853	                (tenant,),
854	            ).fetchall()
855	            for row in rows:
856	                if not self._within_window(_parse_stored_time(row["triggered_at"]), since, until):
857	                    continue
858	                triggers[row["workflow_id"]] = triggers.get(row["workflow_id"], 0) + row["count"]
859	
860	        return {
861	            "status_distribution": distribution,
862	            "node_completions": dict(sorted(completions.items())),
863	            "node_failures": dict(sorted(failures.items())),
864	            "retry_consumption": dict(sorted(retries.items())),
865	            "delivery_succeeded": succeeded,
866	            "delivery_failed": failed,
867	            "schedule_triggers": dict(sorted(triggers.items())),
868	        }
869	
870	    @staticmethod
871	    def _within_window(occurred_at: datetime, since: datetime | None, until: datetime | None) -> bool:
872	        """Closed-interval membership: a fact equal to either endpoint counts."""
873	        if since is not None and occurred_at < since:
874	            return False
875	        if until is not None and occurred_at > until:
876	            return False
877	        return True

879	    def metrics_export(
880	        self,
881	        tenant: str,
882	        since: datetime | None = None,
883	        until: datetime | None = None,
884	    ) -> str:
885	        """Render the filtered metrics in the Prometheus text exposition format.
886	
887	        Every top-level dimension is one metric family named with the
888	        ``chronicleflow_`` prefix and the dimension's public key. Families
889	        appear in the documented top-level key order; samples within a family
890	        are ordered by ascending label value. Every family carries at least
891	        one zero-valued sample when it has no facts, values are decimal
892	        integers, every line ends with a newline, and the whole document ends
893	        with a single newline.
894	        """
895	        counts = self.metrics(tenant, since, until)
896	        status = counts["status_distribution"]
897	        terminated = status["terminated"]
898	        # Samples order by their label values: status first (completed, running,
899	        # then the terminated samples by ascending reason), which is the
900	        # ascending tuple-of-label-values order.
901	        lines: list[str] = [
902	            'chronicleflow_status_distribution{status="completed"} ' + str(status["completed"]),
903	            'chronicleflow_status_distribution{status="running"} ' + str(status["running"]),
904	        ]
905	        for reason in TERMINATION_REASONS:
906	            lines.append(
907	                f'chronicleflow_status_distribution{{status="terminated",reason="{reason}"}} '
908	                + str(terminated[reason])
909	            )
910	        for key in ("node_completions", "node_failures", "retry_consumption"):
911	            groups = counts[key]
912	            if groups:
913	                for label_value, value in groups.items():
914	                    lines.append(
915	                        f'chronicleflow_{key}{{node="{_prometheus_label(label_value)}"}} {value}'
916	                    )
917	            else:
918	                # A family with no facts still exposes one zero-valued sample.
919	                lines.append(f"chronicleflow_{key} 0")
920	        lines.append("chronicleflow_delivery_succeeded " + str(counts["delivery_succeeded"]))
921	        lines.append("chronicleflow_delivery_failed " + str(counts["delivery_failed"]))
922	        triggers = counts["schedule_triggers"]
923	        if triggers:
924	            for label_value, value in triggers.items():
925	                lines.append(
926	                    f'chronicleflow_schedule_triggers{{workflow="{_prometheus_label(label_value)}"}} {value}'
927	                )
928	        else:
929	            lines.append("chronicleflow_schedule_triggers 0")
930	        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

951	    def create_workflow(self, raw: Any, key: str | None, tenant: str = DEFAULT_TENANT) -> dict[str, Any]:
952	        subscriptions = None
953	        schedule = None
954	        version = None
955	        if isinstance(raw, dict):
956	            # The version tag, subscriptions, and the schedule are validated
957	            # up front so an invalid declaration rejects the whole request
958	            # before anything is written.
959	            if "version" in raw:
960	                version = _identifier(raw["version"], "version")
961	                raw = {field: value for field, value in raw.items() if field != "version"}
962	            if "subscriptions" in raw:
963	                subscriptions = parse_subscriptions(raw["subscriptions"])
964	                raw = {field: value for field, value in raw.items() if field != "subscriptions"}
965	            if "schedule" in raw:
966	                schedule = parse_schedule(raw["schedule"])
967	                raw = {field: value for field, value in raw.items() if field != "schedule"}
968	        workflow = Workflow.parse(raw)
969	
970	        def create() -> dict[str, Any]:
971	            existing = self.store.connection.execute(
972	                "SELECT current_version FROM workflows WHERE tenant = ? AND id = ?",
973	                (tenant, workflow.id),
974	            ).fetchone()
975	            if existing is not None:
976	                # An untagged post to an existing workflow is always an
977	                # identifier conflict, whether or not the workflow is versioned.
978	                if version is None:
979	                    raise ConflictError(f"workflow {workflow.id} already exists")
980	                duplicate = self.store.connection.execute(
981	                    "SELECT 1 FROM workflow_versions WHERE tenant = ? AND workflow_id = ? AND version = ?",
982	                    (tenant, workflow.id, version),
983	                ).fetchone()
984	                if duplicate:
985	                    raise ConflictError(f"workflow {workflow.id} version {version} already exists")
986	                position_row = self.store.connection.execute(
987	                    "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(position), 0) + 1 AS position FROM workflow_versions "
988	                    "WHERE tenant = ? AND workflow_id = ?",
989	                    (tenant, workflow.id),
990	                ).fetchone()
991	                self._insert_workflow_version(workflow.id, version, position_row["position"], workflow, tenant)
992	                # The newest declared version becomes the current snapshot; the
993	                # versions table keeps every prior revision immutable.
994	                self.store.connection.execute(
995	                    "UPDATE workflows SET document = ?, current_version = ? WHERE tenant = ? AND id = ?",
996	                    (self.store.encode(workflow.as_dict()), version, tenant, workflow.id),
997	                )
998	                self._replace_workflow_subscriptions(workflow.id, version, subscriptions, tenant)
999	                self._register_queue_targets("workflow", workflow.id, subscriptions, tenant)
1000	                if schedule is not None:
1001	                    self._insert_schedule(workflow.id, schedule, tenant)
1002	                # An added version is itself one workflow creation, so it is
1003	                # metered exactly like the first definition.
1004	                self._record_usage(tenant, USAGE_TYPE_WORKFLOW_CREATED)
1005	                result = workflow.as_dict()
1006	                result["version"] = version
1007	                return result
1008	            # A duplicate identifier does not grow the holding, so it keeps the
1009	            # ordinary identifier conflict even when the tenant is at quota.
1010	            self._assert_within_quota(tenant, "workflows")
1011	            try:
1012	                self.store.connection.execute(
1013	                    "INSERT INTO workflows(tenant, id, document, current_version) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
1014	                    (tenant, workflow.id, self.store.encode(workflow.as_dict()), version),
1015	                )
1016	            except Exception as error:
1017	                if "UNIQUE constraint" in str(error):
1018	                    raise ConflictError(f"workflow {workflow.id} already exists") from error
1019	                raise
